## Answer: $6,748.13 of Luka's $7,000 conversion is taxable income for 2025

The backdoor Roth wasn't tax-free because of the pro-rata rule. On Form 8606, a conversion counts as coming proportionally from all of Luka's traditional IRAs as they stood on 31 Dec 2025, not just the account it came out of. His rollover IRA SYN-12040002 holds pre-tax money with no basis, and it counts. The December 2024 plan kept that account in place ("stays as it is"), and that is why most of the conversion is taxable.

| Form 8606 line | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 – 2025 nondeductible contribution (10 Feb 2025) | $7,000.00 | custodian/transactions.csv |
| 2 – Basis from earlier years | $0.00 | portfolio/tax_profile.json |
| 6 – Traditional IRAs at 31 Dec 2025 | $187,544.92 (SYN-12040002: $42,871.51 Larkspur Core Bond Fund + $142,362.18 Fernhollow Large Cap Index Fund + $2,311.23 cash; SYN-12040003: $0) | custodian/positions.csv, cash.csv |
| 8 – Amount converted (13 Feb 2025) | $7,000.00 | transactions.csv, 1099-R |
| 10 – Nontaxable share | 7,000 / 194,544.92 = 3.598% | computed |
| 11 – Nontaxable part of the conversion | $251.87 | computed |
| **18 – Taxable part of the conversion** | **$6,748.13** | computed |
| **14 – Basis carried to 2026** | **$6,748.13** | computed |

The basis isn't lost: the $6,748.13 carries forward and counts against future withdrawals or conversions. If the preparer rounds the ratio to 0.036, the result is $6,748.00 taxable. The 1099-R shows the full $7,000 in box 2a with "taxable amount not determined" checked, so the taxable figure has to come from Form 8606.

**Cross-checks:**
- The 31 Dec cash in the rollover IRA, plus Q1 2026 activity, equals the cash on the Q1 2026 statement ($2,160.08).
- Q4 2025 fees ($1,436.39 in total) match the standard 1% schedule.
- I didn't check the allocation against the investment policy, because it's outside this question.

**Timing:** the 2025 return was due on the record date (15 April 2026). If it was filed treating the full $7,000 as taxable, or without Form 8606, it needs to be amended.
